title: Finite coefficient extension preserves the uniform Tor interval
statement: Fix finite extensions $E\subset F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with ramification index $e$ defined by $\varpi_E\mathcal O_F=\varpi_F^e\mathcal O_F$, and let $W$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme. For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(W,\mathcal O_E)$ with all reductions of Tor amplitude in one interval $[a,b]$, define $C_{F/E,W}(K)=K\otimes^L_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,W}$. Then every $F$-level reduction of $C_{F/E,W}(K)$ has Tor amplitude in the same interval $[a,b]$. More explicitly, at level $m$ choose $n$ with $en\ge m$; the reduction is $K_n\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{F,m}$, and tensoring with any degree-zero $A_{F,m}$-module $N$ identifies the test with $K_n\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}N$, so no flatness of $A_{F,m}/A_{E,n}$ is required. Use [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] and [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] for the coefficient levels, completeness and derived tensor.

proof.text: At target index m use the already constructed same-level quotient inclusion integralScalarQuotientMap from A_E,(m+1) to A_L,(m+1). The integer inclusion sends the source maximal ideal into the target maximal ideal, so taking the same positive power gives this map without using the ramification equation. The residue characterization of completedCoefficientMap gives the commuting square from the two completions to these finite quotients. Apply derivedReductionComposition to its two paths, and compose one derived associativity isomorphism with the inverse of the other. The named completedDerivedScalarExtension, scalarReductionDerivedExtension and scalarExtensionFunctor are the same universal derived-change-of-rings constructions at these four edges. This gives the natural comparison between target reduction after completed scalar extension and same-level source reduction followed by finite scalar extension. The private helper completedScalarReductionComparison proves this step.

Apply the proved scalarExtension_tor theorem from the scalar-extension functor module to hab m and the same-level quotient inclusion. This theorem tests arbitrary degree-zero target modules after scalar restriction (equivalently extends a bounded flat model in the same interval); it requires neither flatness of the quotient inclusion nor constructibility. It yields exactly the same ordered interval [a,b] for the finite scalar extension of the source reduction.

Transport this Tor predicate to the target reduction through the component at K of the comparison in step 1. Unfold the universal representative test in HasProEtaleTorAmplitude, retain its ordered-interval conjunct, and compose each representative isomorphism with that comparison. Apply the unchanged vanishing test from step 2. Since m was arbitrary, the same interval holds at every target level. No tower reconstruction is needed for this pointwise conclusion.
